What is measurement?
Noticing by eye with no numbers
Using tools to find out how big, how heavy, or how hot something is
Collecting no data at all
Guessing size without a ruler or scale
Measurement uses tools such as rulers, scales, and thermometers to get exact numbers.
Measurements help scientists be precise.
Different tools are used for different measurements.
What is the scientific process?
A single experiment with no question first
A series of steps for investigating a question
A question with no experiment or data collection
A final guess with no observations along the way
The scientific process includes asking a question, making a hypothesis, testing, observing, and drawing conclusions.
It is an organized way to learn.
Each step matters.
What is a control group in an experiment?
A group that usually never changes for any reason
A group in the experiment that you leave unchanged so you can compare results
A group that always changes
An experiment with only one group and no comparison
A control group is left unchanged so you can compare and see what really caused the result.
A control group is part of a strong experiment.
It helps you understand what caused the outcome.
What are data?
Numbers with no link to the experiment
Information collected in an experiment—numbers, observations, and results
Descriptive sentences with no measurements
Early ideas with no lab collection
Data are the information you collect—measurements, observations, and results.
Data help you understand what happened.
Careful data collection is important.
What is a graph?
A decorative drawing with no axes
A chart that shows data visually so patterns are easier to see
A word list with no scale
A column of numbers with no clear trend
A graph shows data visually with lines, bars, or other shapes so trends are easier to spot.
Graphs help people understand data.
There are many kinds of graphs.
What is a conclusion in an experiment?
Opening the report before the experiment
What you learned from the experiment and what the data show
A new question with no link to the data
A guess before checking the graph
A conclusion explains what the data show, whether the hypothesis was supported, and what that means.
Conclusions are an important part of science.
They explain what was learned.
What is a scientific theory?
A guess with no repeated experiments
An explanation of a natural pattern based on many experiments and observations
A philosophy question with no testing
One final word with no support from data
A scientific theory is a well-supported explanation based on lots of evidence—not just a casual guess.
Theories can change when new evidence appears.
That is part of how science works.
What is a scientific law?
A guess about what might happen in a science experiment.
A statement that always and accurately describes how something in nature behaves.
Something that students in a class can change whenever they want.
A sentence written without any evidence or data to support it.
A scientific law is a statement that accurately and consistently describes a natural phenomenon every time. For example, the law of gravity describes how all objects with mass attract each other.
Scientific laws are based on many repeated experiments and observations.
The law of gravity states that all objects with mass attract each other.
What is fertilizer?
Irrigation water with no added minerals
A material added to soil to give plants nutrients
Dry clay with no nitrogen or phosphorus
Sunlight with no soil nutrients
Fertilizer adds nutrients such as nitrogen and phosphorus to soil so plants can grow better.
There are natural and synthetic fertilizers.
Fertilizer can help plants grow stronger.
What does soil provide for plants?
Soil only provides sunlight for plants to grow.
Soil provides nutrients and minerals that plants need to grow, and it holds roots in place.
Soil provides only water and nothing else.
Soil provides only carbon dioxide for photosynthesis.
Soil is rich in nutrients and minerals that plants need. It also holds the roots firmly in place and helps retain water near the roots.
Plant roots absorb water and nutrients from the soil.
Healthy soil contains more nutrients, which helps plants grow better.
What does it mean when a material is biodegradable?
The material is found naturally in soil, just like plastic.
The material breaks down naturally in the environment over time.
The material came from a mountain and is extremely hard.
The material dissolves in water but cannot break down in nature.

A biodegradable material is one that can be broken down by natural processes over time, such as food scraps, paper, or wood. Plastic is not biodegradable and stays in the environment for hundreds of years.
Biodegradable materials like food, paper, and wood decompose naturally.
Non-biodegradable materials like plastic stay in the environment for a very long time.
What is a synthetic material?
A material from stone or wood with no chemical change
A material people make in a factory, not found ready-made in nature
A tree trunk cut exactly as it grew
Pure basalt rock with no processing
Synthetic materials are made by people through industrial processes—plastic and synthetic fibers are examples.
Synthetic materials can be strong and durable.
Some do not break down easily.
What is a dwarf planet?
A heavy body that makes light like the Sun
A body that orbits a star and is between a planet and an asteroid in size
Usually a natural moon of a planet
A body with an icy tail near the Sun
A dwarf planet orbits a star. It is smaller than a regular planet but larger than a typical asteroid. Pluto is an example.
The solar system has several dwarf planets.
This is a fairly recent classification.
What is a gas giant planet?
A small rocky planet like Earth, with solid ground to walk on.
A very large planet made mostly of gas, with no solid surface.
Any body in space that orbits the Moon.
A planet made entirely of solid rock deep inside.
Gas giants are very large planets made mostly of gases. Jupiter and Saturn are examples of gas giants in our solar system.
Gas giants like Jupiter and Saturn are the largest planets in our solar system.
Strong gravity holds the thick layers of gas together in a gas giant.
What is renewable energy?
Energy from a limited source that can run out
Energy from sunlight, wind, or water that nature keeps renewing
Energy from swapping limited oil stores
Energy from burning coal
Renewable energy comes from sources that do not run out, such as sunlight, wind, and flowing water. It is cleaner than oil and coal.
Renewable energy helps protect the environment.
It is part of living more sustainably.
What is electronic waste?
A pile of recycled office paper
Waste from old electronic devices such as computers, phones, and TVs
Empty kitchen plastic bottles
Glass jars from paper recycling
Electronic waste comes from old devices. Recycling it matters because it can contain both hazardous and valuable materials.
E-waste is a growing modern problem.
Recycling electronics is important.
What is a double-blind experiment?
An experiment with only one group
An experiment in which neither the participant nor the researcher knows who got which treatment
A series of experiments where everyone knows the treatment
An observation with no comparison to a controlled condition
In a double-blind experiment, neither the participant nor the researcher knows who received the real treatment or the placebo. That reduces bias.
Double-blind design is an important scientific method.
It helps keep results fair and objective.
What is a sample in an experiment?
The entire population with no filtering
A smaller group you test in order to learn about a larger group
A single participant with no generalizing
Writing a question with no data collection
A sample is a smaller group studied to learn about a larger group—for example, testing 100 plants to learn about many plants.
A sample should represent the larger group well.
Sampling saves time and resources.
What happens to a plant when it does not get enough light?
It boosts photosynthesis until it no longer needs water
It becomes weak, turns yellow, and does not grow well
It rushes into blooming with no leaves
Its cell walls thicken at once with no water loss
Without enough light, a plant cannot photosynthesize well, so it weakens, yellows, and grows poorly.
Light is very important for plants.
Without light, a plant cannot make food.
Why are plants important for life on Earth?
Plants are not important — animals could survive without them.
Plants produce oxygen and provide food for animals and other living things.
Plants are important only because they perform photosynthesis in science labs.
Plants are important only because they store extra food underground.
Plants are essential: they produce the oxygen we breathe through photosynthesis and serve as the base of most food chains on Earth.
Without plants, most life on Earth could not survive.
Plants are producers — they make food using sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide.
What is the difference between a hard material and a soft material?
Hardness depends only on color, not on resistance to scratching
A hard material is difficult to press or cut; a soft material is easy to press and change shape
A soft material is always easier to smash than metal and never returns to shape
A hard material is always struck without absorbing any energy
Hard materials resist pressing, cutting, and breaking (like stone). Soft materials are easy to press and reshape (like cotton).
Every material has different properties.
Hardness is one of those properties.
What is true about how materials let light through?
No material ever allows light to pass through it.
Some materials let light through (like glass), while others block it (like wood).
All materials always let all light pass through them completely.
Whether light passes through a material depends only on the material's color.

Materials that let light pass through are called transparent (like glass). Materials that block light entirely are called opaque (like wood). Some let only a little light through — those are translucent.
Transparent materials allow light to pass through completely.
Opaque materials block all light, and translucent materials let only some light through.
What are the stars in the night sky?
Tiny dots with no energy source
Huge, very distant stars that make their own light and look like points from Earth
Moons that reflect light like the Sun
Planets that glow exactly like stars at night
Night-sky stars are huge glowing balls of gas. They look tiny because they are extremely far away.
They are part of our galaxy.
There are millions of stars.
What is a star?
A large rocky body that orbits a planet.
A giant ball of hot glowing gas that produces its own light and heat.
A chunk of rock that orbits Earth like the Moon.
A cold, dark object that reflects light from the Sun.
A star is a massive ball of hot gas held together by gravity. Inside a star, nuclear reactions release huge amounts of energy as light and heat. The Sun is the closest star to Earth.
Stars appear as tiny points of light because they are extremely far away from Earth.
There are billions of stars in our galaxy alone, and the universe contains billions of galaxies.
Why is it important to protect the environment?
Because pollution always disappears by itself in hours with no action
So nature, animals, and plants can stay healthy
Because there are usually many people in an area
Because there is a place with water
Protecting the environment helps keep nature healthy so people can breathe clean air, drink clean water, and live in a cleaner world.
It matters for everyone alive today.
It also matters for future generations.
